summary: Invisible three-row text window: a Ui_Object-derived window whose InitPanes reserves three blank text rows ('null_txt_l1'..'null_txt_l3') at row tags 0..2 so another window can fill them later.
evidence: Ui_ThreeRowNullTextWindow_Ctor (0x003B578C) allocates through Ui_Object_CtorBase (0x001A66A0) and stores vtable 0x00768C00 at +0. InitPanes (0x003B56A8, vtable slot +0x38 of the base window vtable) calls the virtual text-layer creator at vtable+0x38 three times with 'null_txt_l1', 'null_txt_l2', 'null_txt_l3' and tag (u16)*(self+0x28)<<16 | row, then vtable+0x48. Dtor 0x003B57A4 is Ui_Object_DtorBase+free. The batch offsets 0xE0/0x120 are virtual call slots +0x38/+0x48, not data members.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ctor 0x003B578C stores DAT_003b57a0 (=0x00768C00, the class vtable) at *self; dtor 0x003B57A4 runs Ui_Object_DtorBase.

fields.name: paneSetId
fields.evidence: asm 0x003B56D4: ldrh r0,[r4,#0x28]; the value is shifted left 16 and OR-ed with the row index to form the 32-bit text-layer id passed to the virtual creator. Same field and name in 11 other UI windows (Ui_StatusParamWindow, Ui_ProfileWindow).

fields.name: unknown_vcall38
fields.evidence: Not a data field: the batch matched `(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x38))(self, name, tag, ...)` (a virtual call through the vptr) and scaled the int* param by 4 (0x38*4 = 0xE0). asm 0x003B5708: ldr ip,[r2,#0x38]; blx ip. Only the batch offset is recorded; treat the bytes at 0xE0 as inherited/unknown.

fields.name: unknown_vcall48
fields.evidence: Not a data field: `(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x48))(param_1, tag)` is the layout-finish virtual call; the extractor scaled slot 0x48 by 4 to 0x120. No data access at 0x120 exists in this function.

summary: Title text window: binds the 'txt_title' and 'txt' panes and owns an embedded message/paging widget at +0x918 plus an embedded layout object at +0xBC8.
evidence: InitPanes 0x0032E5A0 (vtable 0x007644D4 slot +0x1C) binds 'txt_title' and 'txt'; InitPanesC 0x00386940 binds 'txt_title' with tag|0x100. The recovered ctor 0x003868B4 selects the embedded widget with Ui_SelectElement(self, self+0x918) (0x00259928), configures it with FUN_001dab30(self+0x918, ...) and finally makes a virtual call through the embedded object at self+0xBC8 (slot +0x18). NotifyAdvance 0x00387058 advances a ring-buffer cursor, consistent with paging through title pages. Batch offset 0xD0 is vtable slot +0x34, not a field; 3020 is a lower bound (the +0xBC8 object is only partly covered).

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Every instance of this window family is polymorphic: InitPanes and InitPanesC dispatch through *self (slots +0x34/+0x1C), and the related class vtable in structs.json is 0x007644D4. No explicit vptr store appears in the recovered ctor, so 0.85 rather than 0.9.

fields.name: paneSetId
fields.evidence: InitPanes builds every pane tag as (u32)*(u16*)(self+0x28) << 16 | row (0x0032E5A0: `(uint)*(ushort *)(param_1 + 10) << 0x10`), the same pane-id base used by the other Ui text windows.

fields.name: unknown_vcall34
fields.evidence: Not a data field: the evidence line `(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x34))(param_1,0x32e610,...)` is a virtual call through the vptr; the extractor scaled slot 0x34 by 4 to 0xD0.

fields.name: messageWidget
fields.evidence: Ctor 0x003868B4: Ui_SelectElement(self, self+0x918) then FUN_001dab30(self+0x918, FUN_001f0be4(0x1e)). The same two calls name +0x918 'messageWidget' in Ui_TalkWindow; sibling state functions call Ui_Widget_Update(self+0x918, ...). First word of an embedded widget; only 4 bytes are covered by the evidence.

fields.name: maybe_layoutRoot
fields.evidence: Ctor 0x003868B4 ends with a virtual call `(**(code **)(*(int*)(self+0xbc8) + 0x18))(self+0xbc8, 0)`, i.e. +0xBC8 is the first word (vptr) of an embedded layout object whose slot +0x18 is invoked with 0. The same offset is called 'layoutRoot' for Ui_ActionWindow; no full class evidence yet, so u32 + maybe_.

summary: Numbered placeholder text window: InitPanes fills a grid of blank rows whose two-character layer numbers are incremented per row.
evidence: InitPanes 0x003D6988 calls the virtual text creators at vtable+0x34 and +0x38 in a loop (uVar2 0..8), incrementing the digit buffers built from 'null_txt_l1' ('00'..'99') so every row gets a unique layer name; the tag is (u16)*(self+0x28)<<16 | row and vtable+0x48 finishes the layout. Dtor 0x003D6B04 is Ui_Object_DtorBase + free; class vtable 0x0076A394. Batch offsets 0xD0/0xE0/0x120 are virtual call slots +0x34/+0x38/+0x48, not data members.

summary: HUD speech-balloon window: owns an embedded UI object at +0x138 that receives the 'hud_balloon' pane and whose visibility is toggled.
evidence: BindLayout 0x001F3EA8 sets +0x108 = 1, calls Ui_Widget_FindPaneAndNotify(self, self+0x138, 'hud_balloon', 0) and then Gfx_Node_SetVisible(self+0x138, 0). The layout is the same as Ui_FadeWindow, whose dtors prove that +0x138 is an embedded Ui_Object (Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub + Ui_Object_DtorBase on self+0x138). 316 is a lower bound: the embedded object extends past +0x138.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: G_052 names 0x0075B3EC g_uiBalloonWindowVtable, installed at object+0 by the window ctor; BindLayout dispatches through *self (0x001D85EC reads the vptr).

fields.evidence: First statement of BindLayout 0x001F3EA8: *(u8*)(self+0x108) = 1; the same pane-built flag at +0x108 is named isLayoutReady in Ui_BattleTargetWindow and has the identical write in Ui_ShopWindow.

fields.name: embeddedObject
fields.evidence: Ui_Widget_FindPaneAndNotify(self, self+0x138, 'hud_balloon', 0) makes self+0x138 the pane receiver (its vtable +0x20 gets the pane); Gfx_Node_SetVisible(self+0x138, 0) toggles it. Ui_FadeWindow uses the same member and its dtor calls Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub/Ui_Object_DtorBase on +0x138, proving it is an embedded Ui_Object. Only the first word is covered.

summary: Small child window that owns two adjacent 0x50-byte layout-reference groups at +0x58 and +0xA8; both destructors release them before the base UI object is destroyed.
evidence: Ui_ChildWindow_Dtor 0x0047C1B8 and DtorDelete 0x0047C18C store the vtable at +0 (`str r1,[r0],#0xa8`), then call Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self+0xA8), Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self+0x58) and Ui_Object_DtorBase(self); DtorDelete also frees. The two releases are 0x50 bytes apart, so the object is at least 0xF8 bytes (batch size 172 was only highest-strong-field+4).

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Both dtors begin with `str r1,[r0],#0xa8` (asm 0x0047C190 / 0x0047C1BC): store the vtable argument at offset 0, then advance to the +0xA8 layout ref. The batch did not resolve the vtable address, so the type is void*.

fields.name: layoutRef
fields.evidence: Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self+0xA8) (0x003E04BC) releases the second of two 0x50-byte layout-reference groups (the other at +0x58); the returned pointer minus 0x50 is the next group and minus its offset is self. Same offset/type convention as Ui_SingleLayoutObject's layoutRef.

summary: End-credits text window: a window object that constructs one embedded slot panel at +0x11C; the panel owns two 0x50-byte animation-reference groups and a three-word text-handle array.
evidence: Ui_CreditTextWindow_Ctor 0x002880A8 allocates the window with 0x001D8B6C, stores the vtable at +0, constructs a SlotPanel in place at self+0x11C via maybe_Ui_SlotPanel_Ctor 0x0032A2C0 and then builds three 4-byte entries at panel+0x104 with std_ConstructArray. The panel starts with two Ui_AnimRefList groups at +0x4C/+0x9C and writes cleared words up to panel+0x100 and the 3-word array at +0x104, so the object reaches at least 0x11C + 0x110 = 0x22C = 556. The batch base Ui_SlotPanel is a false positive: the SlotPanel ctor is called on self+0x11C (a member), not on self, so base is cleared here.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ctor 0x002880A8 stores the class vtable literal uRam002880e8 at *self immediately after the FUN_001D8B6C allocation; the literal address is not resolved in symbols.json.

fields.name: maybe_slotPanel
fields.evidence: maybe_Ui_SlotPanel_Ctor (0x0032A2C0) is called with self+0x11C and constructs in place: vtable, Ui_AnimRefList at panel+0x4C and panel+0x9C, then the caller builds 3 x 4-byte entries at panel+0x104. The concrete panel class is still uncertain (R3_024 conf 0.45), hence maybe_.

summary: Effect-icon strip window: owns seven 0x50-byte animation-reference groups, one per effect icon slot ('effect0'..'effect6').
evidence: InitPanes 0x003D4600 binds self+0x4C+i*0x50 with Ui_AnimRef_Bind(..., 'effect%d') for i = 0..6 and resets each group; dtor 0x003D46DC runs std_destroy_range(self+0x4C, 0x003E04BC Ui_LayoutRef_Release, 0x50, 7) then Ui_Object_DtorBase + free. The asm loop (mov r2,#0x50; add r0,r4,#0x4C; 7 iterations) fixes the stride/count, so the object reaches 0x4C + 7*0x50 = 0x27C = 636 bytes.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Dtor 0x003D46DC stores DAT_003d4710 (=0x00769E74, leading word of class vtable 0x00769E78) at *self; structs.json vtable 0x00769E78 lists Ui_EffectIconsWindow_Dtor and Ui_EffectIconsWindow_InitPanes.

fields.name: effectIconAnimRefs

Element type Ui_AnimRefList is the 0x50-byte group class used for the same destroy/release pattern in S_013/S_014.

summary: Eight-slot window: owns eight adjacent 0x50-byte animation-reference groups destroyed as one array.
evidence: Dtor 0x004D6B7C installs vtable 0x00779DCC at +0, runs std_destroy_range(self+0x58, 0x003E04BC Ui_LayoutRef_Release, 0x50, 8) then Ui_Object_DtorBase + free. asm 0x004D6B98: add r0,r4,#0x58; mov r2,#0x50; mov r3,#8. The object therefore reaches 0x58 + 8*0x50 = 0x2D8 = 728 bytes (batch had only 92).

fields.name: vtable

fields.name: slotAnimRefs

summary: Screen fade window: owns an embedded Ui_Object at +0x138 that receives the 'win_fade' pane and is shown/hidden to drive the fade.

summary: Five-row window: owns five adjacent 0x50-byte animation-reference groups constructed and destroyed as one array.
